title: A Good Shared Randomness String
statement: Let $L$ and $C$ be languages of bit strings, let $f$ map bit strings to bit strings, and let $a,k$ be nonnegative integers. Suppose that for every bit string $x$, a uniformly random string $r$ of length $a(|x|+1)^k$ satisfies $f(\langle x,r\rangle)\in C$ if and only if $x\in L$ with probability at least $2/3$, where $\langle x,r\rangle$ is the pairing encoding described above. For every nonnegative integer $n$, put $M=36(n+1)$ and $q=a(n+1)^k$. There is a bit string $\rho$ of length $Mq$ such that, for every bit string $v$ of length $n$, membership $v\in L$ is equivalent to more than half of the $M$ strings formed by taking the $q$-bit blocks of $\rho$ (starting with block $i$ for each $0\le i<M$) making $f(\langle v,\text{block}_i\rangle)$ belong to $C$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps bit strings to bit strings
